# Prospective resource and guard controls

Exact literal storage uses one logical request on an empty Vec per literal, with kind `array HIR elements`, N equal to the source element count, including N=0. It checks N<=1024, shared cumulative requested-entry addition, and N times measured ExprId width before reserving. It uses the existing Allocator request/failure/trace machinery and real `try_reserve_exact`, not `try_reserve`, collect, clone or raw-lowering allocation mapping. Requested N is not claimed allocator capacity. The vector fills only admitted slots. Nested-literal requests occur outer before inner, although retained HIR IDs are postorder. The counter does not reset across functions or modules.

Freeze errors: E0400/resolve, full literal origin, no notes/secondaries, exact text `array HIR count overflow` or `array HIR allocation failed`. Resource JSON contains exact rendered bytes at each selected literal. Run a real fallible injected reservation error at every new request (including zero), recording actual allocator attempt/event; independently test checked cumulative/multiplication/attempt-counter overflow. Synthetic overflow is neither natural valid-source overflow nor OOM evidence. No expected N/error/origin enters the compiler; array-relative fault ordinals may be translated to allocator attempts by a bounded test harness, and every earlier actual request is retained in the receipt. No qualifying semantic result can be inferred from a failed construction.

Added work contract, frozen prospectively from the accepted design and the producer's pre-observation interface proposal:

- Resolve: 1 unit for each ArrayLiteral, IndexRead, ArrayLength and IndexAssign before node-specific inspection; 1 unit for each literal edge before recursively resolving that child
- Type: 1 unit for each ArrayLiteral, IndexRead, ArrayLength and IndexAssign before its array-specific inspection; 1 unit for each literal edge before recursively typing that child; a seeded empty leaf charges its literal-node unit exactly once
- Array access: 1 unit immediately before O(1) initialized binding-kind inspection for each read, write or length, after required operand typing
- Annotated fixed-array initializer peel: 1 unit before each examined node's kind, counting each Group and the final non-Group leaf exactly once; only complete annotated local initializer paths are eligible

All charges use the same nonresetting WorkMeter as source/index work. Existing name/type/query/I/J/W admission order and charges remain unchanged. The added successful-run total is R_nodes + E_ast + T_nodes + E_ast + accesses + peeled_examined_nodes. This does not assert that all legacy resolve work was metered. The external resource checker derives the actual traversal prefix on failure from source and the prescribed schedule, accounts legacy charges separately, and binds that reviewed ledger before applying exact-W/one-over/downward controls. It must not define expected W as whatever total a candidate happened to report. For the two-module reserve case, the added total is 16: resolve 4 nodes+3 edges, type 4 nodes+3 edges+2 accesses; no annotated peel. For the grouped-store source the added total is 16: resolve 4 nodes+2 edges, type 4 nodes+2 edges+3 accesses+1 examined annotated initializer leaf. For an annotated empty with two Groups it is 8: resolve 2 nodes, type 2 nodes+1 access+3 peel nodes. These totals exclude all unchanged legacy charges.

Observer traversal and passive traces have a separate ledger. Broad corpus runs cannot enable an unbounded WorkMeter observation log. For small targeted controls, retain a stated finite bound on input nodes and log events; observation allocation never masquerades as compiler admission.

Program guards must run before source-map branching, root-main entry checking, declaration admission, function iteration, counting or output allocation, at checked SourceOwner root EOF. `Walk::new` rejects at checked signature origin before output reservation, inventory, blocks or walk. The same constructor covers both count modes and emission. Guard rows use canonical-site OwnedFailure and the bound existing lower formatter: E0500/oir-owned-lower, `internal compiler error: owned invariant violation`, no secondary/notes. Functions absent is a valid guard test, not a skipped one. Parent-program guards have zero sentinels after typing. Direct function controls may enter their named wrapper, but no counting body/inventory/reserve/emit action may run. Inject a first raw reservation failure concurrently with the guard test to prove the guard still wins; the denial code alone is insufficient. Scalar-selected cases identify the explicit private-owned test seam.

Measure candidate row sizes rather than assuming baseline sizes: Expr/ExprKind, Stmt/StmtKind, Binding/Signature/Function/BodyBlock, resolved and typed owners/views/admission tag, Option/Vec headers, ValueTy/ParameterTy slots and unchanged Projection rows. Record toolchain/target/profile for debug/release and applicable hosts. No expected numeric byte size is frozen here. Source facts (N/E_ast/E_hir/counts/identities) remain separate from Rust layout receipts.

Checked requested payload includes enclosing HIR rows, parameters, old argument and field-init vectors, E_hir times measured ExprId width, typing Option scratch and final vectors during conversion, projection/binding/block-flow scratch, call actuals and bounded recursion/loop frames. Vec headers appear once in enclosing rows. Report live source/AST/index + HIR + typing + observer overlap, including pending literal buffers; attached plus pending requested slots are bounded by source E_ast even when partially filled E_hir is smaller. Accepted complete programs cross-check E_hir=E_ast and HIR-expressions=AST-expressions-target-wrappers, without trusting either equality as an input allocation plan. Derive the finite source-N envelope; no new HIR cap substitutes for existing index or raw caps. Requested payload is not RSS/capacity or universal OOM coverage. Q, lower completion, association, ownership, execution, bounds/fuel and activation remain absent.
